public_health_relevance.quote: WNV is a major cause of mosquito-borne disease in the continental United States (U.S.).

study_design_rigor.justification: This meets the score 3 description: the methods specify sample sources, extraction inputs, sequencing workflows, alignment and consensus thresholds, and in-silico primer criteria. The design includes an RT-dPCR-anchored dilution panel, contemporary and archival samples, technical replicates, and matched three-method comparisons, as illustrated in the workflow on page 19 and reported across Figures 2–5 and Table 1.
study_design_rigor.quote: Two primer pools tiled across the WNV genome (38 amplicons, 76 primers) were generated by one-step multiplex RT-PCR from extracted RNA

results_and_conclusion.justification: This meets the score 3 description: the results are supported by Figures 2–5 and Table 1, include dilution-panel, replicate, matched-method, and in-silico validation, and the stated limitations of the two-donation matched comparison and workflow-specific processing are explicit. Internal numeric checks are consistent: Table 1's shotgun mean recovery of 93.5% matches 99.8% and 87.2%, and its approximately 0.5% mean on-target fraction matches 0.85% and 0.18%; Figure 4 likewise shows the lower-input shotgun result of 87.2%, with no fractional discrete read or sample counts reported.
results_and_conclusion.quote: Consensus-level substitution profiles were identical across sequencing methods for both matched donations

references.justification: The reference list combines foundational WNV epidemiology and transfusion-screening studies, recent WNV genomic-surveillance work, and relevant sequencing, bioinformatics, and phylogenetic-method sources. Most entries are peer-reviewed; the limited use of Nextstrain web material, medRxiv preprints, and an arXiv methods reference is contextually relevant, and no clearly unrelated reference is apparent.
references.quote: Blood donors as sentinels for genomic surveillance of West Nile virus in Germany using a sensitive amplicon-based sequencing approach.
